previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and recent cholangitis treated with meropenem was readmitted for weakness and two falls following discharge. He attributed his lightheadedness to the switch to ertapenem. Orthostatic vitals were normal, and telemetry showed no arrhythmias. He received a small IV fluid bolus and was evaluated by physical therapy, who recommended a cane and home safety evaluation. Given his clinical improvement and completion of 10 days of IV antibiotics, he was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for the remainder of his treatment. Platelet count was elevated but trending down, likely reactive. Liver enzymes and renal function remained stable. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up in the liver clinic and plans for stent removal in six months.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Patient with fever, assess for pneumonia.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Frontal and lateral views of the chest demonstrate low lung volumes, which
accentuate bronchovascular markings.  There are bibasilar opacities, which
project over spine on the lateral view.  Hilar and mediastinal silhouettes are
unremarkable.  There is pulmonary vascular congestion.  Heart size is top
normal.  No pleural effusion.  The biliary drains are in place.

IMPRESSION:

Bibasilar opacities may represent atelectasis or infection in the appropriate
clinical setting.  Pulmonary vascular congestion.

INDICATION:  Altered mental status.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired contiguous images through the head were obtained
without intravenous contrast at 5-mm slice thickness.  Coronally and
sagittally reformatted images are provided.

FINDINGS:

There is no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or shift
of normally midline structures.  There is no cerebral edema or gray-white
matter differentiation to suggest an acute ischemic event.  The sulci and
ventricles are prominent, likely age-related involutional changes.  Again
noted prominent ventricles relative to sulcal enlargement.  Confluent
periventricular hypodensities, likely reflect sequela of small vessel ischemic
disease.  The orbits are unremarkable.  No acute fracture is seen.  Imaged
paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well aerated.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of acute intracranial process.

INDICATION:  Patient with history of liver transplant, assess for ascites or
liver abscess.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

FINDINGS:

The liver demonstrates coarse echotexture without suspicious focal lesions. 
The left hepatic lobe remains atrophic.  No clear intrahepatic biliary ductal
dilatation is demonstrated.  Gallbladder is surgically absent.  The portal
vasculature appears patent.  The main portal and right portal veins appear
patent with appropriate waveforms.  The left portal vein is not clearly
visualized.  The middle, left and right hepatic veins demonstrate appropriate
waveforms.  The main hepatic artery demonstrates appropriate arterial waveform
with variable velocities.  There is no ascites.  The IVC is patent.

IMPRESSION:  

Patent hepatic vasculature.  No ascites or discrete hepatic mass lesion.
